basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 5.' and it opens 'Vers. 5. Sanguinem de manu bestiarum requiram. Bestiam vocat crudeles homines et feros.'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 5. Sanguinem de manu bestiarum requiram. Bestiam vocat crudeles homines et feros. De manu viri et fratris ejus. Fratrem vocat omnem hominem ejusdem consortem naturae.
